source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
That sounds great! Where are you going?

I wanted to get your opinion on a UI/UX design question. At present, the shell/dashboard has a collapsible panel on the left, and some apps may have a collapsible panel of their own; in this example, the app panel is also on the left. If two panels are present—one for the shell and one for the app, perhaps they could be displayed and collapsed on opposite sides of the screen. What do you think of that idea, and which side should each one occupy? My current preference, though it is not decided, is to put the shell panel on the right. I may prototype the different placements so that we can experiment. Any thoughts are welcome.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Your perspective is interesting \[sic\], though in the western world people's attention naturally shifts back to the left-hand side. That makes me think panels on both sides might feel somewhat unnatural.

Although AWS Cognito generates the Sign In page, its styling can be customized; the background I created was intended for that page. To see what I mean, open <https://cdn.lumenarc-demo.example> and select Sign In. That same background is now being used for the Tenant Launch Flow. Its functionality is working, but I still need to revisit the styling, so I probably won't send it to you for 9 days. For the time being, standard pages such as Cookie and Privacy are PDFs that I can simply open in separate tabs.

ambiguity.description: The client now leans away from placing panels on both sides but still does not confirm the proposed nested single-panel structure or another final panel arrangement.
